title: Retraction from a w-local map after restricting to a closed component union
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings with w-local spectra [def-weil-pbc-w-local], and let g:R\to S be a ring map. Assume g is bijective on all prime stalks [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and sends every closed point of Spec S to a closed point of Spec R. Let h:\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}S)\to\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}R) be the map induced by contraction of primes along g, and let T\subseteq\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}S) be closed. If the restriction h|_T:T\to\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}R) is bijective, then there exists a ring map s:S\to R with s\circ g=\mathrm{id}_R.

proof.text: Equip S with the R-algebra structure induced by g. The w-local hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses recorded in [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. The resulting algebra map is g, so its contraction map on prime spectra and on connected components is the given map h.

proof.text: For each prime q of S, the assumed bijection of the canonical localization map R_{g⁻¹(q)} → S_q is precisely bijectivity on the prime stalks of this algebra map. Thus the auxiliary theorem’s stalk hypothesis holds.

proof.text: The assumed closed-point contraction condition is exactly the auxiliary closed-point hypothesis. Since h|_T is bijective, for every component of Spec R there is a component in T mapping to it, and two components in T with the same image are equal; these are the auxiliary surjectivity and injectivity conditions.

proof.text: Apply the closed-component retraction theorem to the algebra map, T, and the three verified hypotheses. It yields a ring map s:S→R with s∘g=id_R.
